issues.body:
WEB_RDF_ACCEPT (import-drawer.tsx:103-107) is passed verbatim to pickTextFiles({accept}), which forwards it into showOpenFilePicker's options.types[].accept (file-ingest.ts:184-192). That API validates each suffix and throws TypeError when a suffix contains a disallowed code point; the permitted set is narrow (ASCII alphanumeric plus '+' and '.'), and '.json-ld' contains a hyphen.

I could not verify the exact code-point rule in this environment (no network), so I am stating this as a concrete risk rather than a confirmed break. But the failure mode is what makes it worth blocking: pickTextFiles catches every non-AbortError and falls back to pickViaInput (file-ingest.ts:205-208), so if the suffix IS rejected, every 'Browse files…' click quietly takes the hidden-input path and the PR's stated goal — 'retain the File System Access API path where available' (import-drawer.tsx:721-722) — is false in the only browser family that ships FSA, with no error surfaced anywhere. The library's own doc comment at file-ingest.ts:168-170 already lists 'option TypeError' as an anticipated failure, which is evidence this is a live hazard rather than a hypothetical one.

Note the accept list is doing double duty: it is both the ingest filter (where '.json-ld' is genuinely useful, since FORMAT_OPTIONS at rdf-format.ts:23 maps 'json-ld' to jsonld) and the picker dialog filter (where it may be illegal). Those two consumers need different treatment.
issues.fix_hint:
Verify first — in a Chrome console run `showOpenFilePicker({types:[{accept:{'text/plain':['.json-ld']}}]})` and see whether it throws TypeError before the dialog opens.

Either way, harden the shared library rather than only the caller: in pickTextFiles, filter opts.accept down to picker-legal suffixes before building `types` (drop any suffix that does not match /^\.[a-z0-9+.]{1,15}$/i after lowercasing), and keep the FULL list for the readFiles extension check so ingest behaviour is unchanged. That keeps '.json-ld' working as an ingest filter, keeps the dialog filter valid, and makes the library robust against any future consumer passing an exotic suffix. Optionally also distinguish a genuine option TypeError from a SecurityError in the catch at file-ingest.ts:205 so a misconfigured accept list is not indistinguishable from an unsupported browser.
issues.title: Adding '.json-ld' to WEB_RDF_ACCEPT may make showOpenFilePicker throw TypeError, silently killing the FSA path this PR exists to restore

issues.body:
The whole point of adding `readFile` to IngestOptions is that a consumer no longer needs its own copy of the ingest loop. handleBrowse now uses it, but handleDrop (import-drawer.tsx:688-718) still duplicates readDroppedFiles verbatim — the items/kind loop, the webkitGetAsEntry directory check, the getAsFile null check, and the two reason strings are copy-pasted from file-ingest.ts:227-252, and readFilesWithDecompress duplicates readFiles.

Most concretely, import-drawer.tsx:607 inlines `unsupported file type — expected ${WEB_RDF_ACCEPT.join(" / ")}` instead of calling the library's rejectedReasonUnsupported (file-ingest.ts:91-93). The two are byte-identical today, so the drop and browse paths agree — but nothing enforces that, and the moment the library message is reworded the same rejected file will report different text depending on how it entered. The identical duplication of the 'could not be read: ' prefix at import-drawer.tsx:617 vs file-ingest.ts:117 has the same hazard, and the new test at file-ingest.test.ts:57-59 pins the library's copy only.
issues.fix_hint:
Replace handleDrop's body and readFilesWithDecompress with a single call:

  void readDroppedFiles(e.dataTransfer, { accept: WEB_RDF_ACCEPT, readFile: decompressReader }).then(onIngest);

and handleInputChange with:

  const result = await readFiles-equivalent — i.e. export a small `readFiles(files, opts)` from file-ingest.ts (it is already the shared helper, just module-private) and call it with the same options object.

That deletes ~35 lines from import-drawer.tsx, removes both duplicated literals, and makes the drop path covered by the new test instead of merely resembling it. If you prefer to keep the local copies, at minimum import and call rejectedReasonUnsupported so the message has one definition.
issues.title: Refactor is half-landed: handleDrop still hand-rolls readDroppedFiles, and duplicates the reject-reason string

issues.body:
The tests are genuinely non-vacuous: test 1 proves the custom reader is used AND the default File.text() is not (the defaultReaderCalled=false assertion is the real mutation guard), test 2 pins the 'could not be read: ' prefix, and test 3 proves the accept filter short-circuits before the reader runs. The fakes are sound — droppedFile() sets items:[] so `dataTransfer.items?.length` is falsy and the FileList branch at file-ingest.ts:249-252 is taken, which is a real path.

But all three go through readDroppedFiles, and import-drawer.tsx does NOT call readDroppedFiles — it hand-rolls the drop path (see the previous finding). The only new production consumer of `readFile` is pickTextFiles via handleBrowse (import-drawer.tsx:723-728), and that has no coverage; neither does the new accept-filter branch added to readFilesWithDecompress (import-drawer.tsx:604-610), which is not exported and therefore not testable at all.

Coverage is real because readFiles is shared by both entry points, so this is a mis-aimed test rather than a fake one — but as written the suite would stay green if handleBrowse's readFile option were dropped entirely.
issues.fix_hint: Add a pickTextFiles case covering the option that actually changed. It is testable in Node without a DOM: stub globalThis.window with a showOpenFilePicker returning a fake handle whose getFile() resolves the fake File, stub globalThis.document, then assert the custom readFile ran and the default File.text() did not — mirroring test 1. Also add one case asserting a File System Access handle whose getFile() rejects lands in `rejected` with the 'could not be read: ' prefix (file-ingest.ts:196-202), which is currently uncovered. If you collapse handleDrop onto readDroppedFiles per the previous finding, the existing three tests then cover the drop path for real.
issues.title: New tests exercise readDroppedFiles, which the import drawer does not call — the changed production path is untested

issues.body:
Before this PR the drop path applied no extension filter — every dropped file went straight to maybeDecompressFile, and guessFormat's fallback (rdf-format.ts:62) parsed unknown extensions as turtle. The new check at import-drawer.tsx:604 rejects anything outside the 15-entry list, so files that previously imported successfully — .n3, .rdf, .owl, and any RDF file with a non-standard or absent extension — now fail with 'unsupported file type'. Tightening the filter is a defensible choice and arguably the intent, but it is a user-visible behaviour change that the PR description and gui/README.md do not mention.

The sharper problem is .hdt. The pane copy at import-drawer.tsx:741-743 prominently promises 'Native-only HDT archives (.hdt) still require the desktop app', and guessFormat/isHdt (rdf-format.ts:47-50, 58) have dedicated HDT handling. But .hdt is not in WEB_RDF_ACCEPT, so a dropped .hdt now produces the generic 'unsupported file type — expected .ttl / .turtle / ...' — the one case where the UI has already told the user a specific, actionable answer, and the filter throws it away.
issues.fix_hint:
Special-case HDT before the generic accept check in readFilesWithDecompress:

  if (isHdt(file.name)) { rejected.push({ name: file.name, reason: "HDT archives are native-only — open this file in the desktop app" }); continue; }

(isHdt is already exported from rdf-format.ts and correctly handles .hdt.gz.)

Separately, decide deliberately about the tightening: either widen WEB_RDF_ACCEPT with the other extensions the engine can actually parse as turtle (.n3, .rdf, .owl), or note the intentional narrowing in gui/README.md so the behaviour change is recorded rather than incidental.
issues.title: New drop-path accept filter rejects files that previously imported, and gives .hdt a message contradicting the pane's own copy

issues.body:
maybeDecompressFile returns MaybeDecompressedFile with an `effectiveName` field that exists precisely so the caller can detect format from the INNER name (file-decompress.ts:22-27, 122-123). decompressReader (import-drawer.tsx:597-598) throws it away and returns only `.text`, because IngestOptions.readFile is typed `(file: File) => Promise<string>`.

Downstream, format is chosen by guessFormat(file.name) at import-drawer.tsx:271 — the OUTER name. That recovers correctly for .gz/.bz2/.zst/.zstd only, because COMPRESSION_EXTS (rdf-format.ts:28) contains exactly those four. But WEB_RDF_ACCEPT also admits .zip, .tgz, .gzip and .bzip2, none of which stripCompression strips. So `data.nq.zip` yields ext 'zip', no FORMAT_OPTIONS hit, and the turtle fallback — an N-Quads or JSON-LD payload handed to the turtle parser.

This is pre-existing (the old readFilesWithDecompress discarded decoded.effectiveName the same way) and is NOT a regression, so it is not a blocker for this PR. I raise it because this PR is the one that fixes the shape of the reader contract into the shared library, and the string-only signature makes the bug unfixable at the library level for every future consumer.
issues.fix_hint:
Widen the hook now while it has exactly one caller:

  readFile?: (file: File) => Promise<string | { text: string; effectiveName?: string }>

and in readFiles (file-ingest.ts:113) push `name: result.effectiveName ?? file.name` when the object form comes back. Then decompressReader can return the whole MaybeDecompressedFile and `data.nq.zip` is imported as nquads. Alternatively, leave the signature alone and add 'zip', 'tgz', 'gzip', 'bzip2' to COMPRESSION_EXTS — but that is wrong for containers, since stripping '.zip' from 'archive.zip' yields no inner extension at all. The effectiveName route is the correct one. Either way this is fine to land as a follow-up bead.
issues.title: readFile's string-only return type discards effectiveName, so zip/tgz archives get the wrong RDF format

issues.body:
pickViaInput resolves only on 'change' or 'cancel' (file-ingest.ts:153-160). The 'cancel' event on <input type="file"> is relatively recent; on engines that do not fire it, a user who opens the dialog and dismisses it leaves the promise pending forever, and the hidden input has already been appended to document.body.

Previously handleBrowse just called inputRef.current.click() and returned synchronously, so this could not happen on this path. It is harmless in practice — handleBrowse sets no busy flag, so nothing locks up and the button stays usable — which is why this is a nit rather than a real defect. The cost is a small leak (a detached-but-appended input plus a retained closure) per dismissed dialog.
issues.fix_hint: Nothing required for this PR. If you want to close it in the library, add a one-shot window 'focus' listener alongside the 'cancel' listener in pickViaInput: on focus return, defer a tick and, if no 'change' has fired, resolve emptyResult() and remove the input. That is the standard workaround and preserves the no-silent-drop invariant, since a cancel legitimately means nothing was selected.
issues.title: handleBrowse now awaits a promise that can never settle when the browser does not fire the input 'cancel' event

issues.body:
Three small staleness points left by the change:

1. The README sentence is accurate but buries the new option mid-clause; readFile is a public API addition to IngestOptions and deserves its own mention in the 'Entry points' paragraph rather than a parenthetical, since it is what makes binary consumers possible at all.

2. import-drawer.tsx:593-595 still says readFilesWithDecompress 'Replaces the readDroppedFiles / File.text() call paths in the web-upload pane' — the browse path now goes through pickTextFiles, not this helper, so the comment describes a scope the function no longer wholly owns.

3. The drop-zone hint at import-drawer.tsx:776-778 lists '.ttl · .nt · .nq · .trig · .jsonld · .gz · .zip · .zst · .bz2' and was not updated for the newly accepted .turtle / .ntriples / .nquads / .json-ld aliases. Users now get 'unsupported file type' listing 15 extensions when the visible hint advertises 9 — the filter and the hint disagree in both directions.
issues.fix_hint: Update the hint text to match WEB_RDF_ACCEPT (or derive it from the constant so it cannot drift), and reword the import-drawer.tsx:593 doc comment to say the helper serves the input and drop paths while the browse path uses pickTextFiles with the same decompressReader. In gui/README.md, give readFile its own sentence in the Entry points paragraph noting the default is File.text() and that the Import drawer overrides it with maybeDecompressFile.
issues.title: Doc drift: helper comment and drop-zone hint text not updated for the new behaviour

verdict.summary:
The change is directionally right and internally coherent: adding an optional `readFile` hook to the shared ingest library lets `handleBrowse` keep the File System Access path while still decompressing archives, and the expanded WEB_RDF_ACCEPT aliases (.turtle/.ntriples/.nquads/.json-ld) now line up exactly with FORMAT_OPTIONS in rdf-format.ts, so guessFormat recognises everything the filter admits. The new accept-filter in readFilesWithDecompress upholds the no-silent-drop invariant, and the new test is NOT vacuous (it pins reader delegation, the 'could not be read: ' prefix, and that a rejected extension short-circuits before the reader).

The blocking concern is that the same PR that restores the FSA path may disable it: showOpenFilePicker validates every suffix in options.types[].accept and throws TypeError on invalid code points, and the newly added '.json-ld' contains a hyphen, whose validity I could not confirm (no network in this environment). pickTextFiles swallows that TypeError into the hidden-input fallback, so if the hyphen is rejected, every Browse click silently degrades in the only browser family that ships FSA — with zero signal. The library's own doc comment already names 'option TypeError' as an expected failure, which is exactly why it should sanitise suffixes rather than trust consumer lists.

Secondary completeness gaps: the refactor is half-landed (handleDrop + readFilesWithDecompress still hand-roll readDroppedFiles, including a duplicated reject-reason literal that will drift from rejectedReasonUnsupported); the new test aims at readDroppedFiles, which the drawer does not call, leaving the actual new production path untested; and the new drop-path filter rejects files that previously imported fine, giving .hdt a generic message that contradicts the pane's own 'HDT requires the desktop app' copy.

No security issues: reject reasons flow into React text nodes (escaped), and the diff contains no text directed at the reviewer.
